Brave advertises that you can replace ads and then share in the revenue generated from those ads. Maybe this is something they're planning in the future, but as of right now there is no option for revenue sharing.

There is no option to clear history and browsing data like there is in other browsers. I like to do this periodically just in case a tracking cookie gets through but there's no way to do it in Brave.

It's VERY basic as far as features and things. This makes for a nice minimalistic interface, but it often feels like some features are missing.

The navigation bar shows the page title when you mouse away from it, which is a cool feature. But the title shows in the navigation bar and still shows in the normal title bar. So it's showing in two places, which sort of defeats the purpose.

Page loading seems to be pretty fast compared to Firefox. I think comparable with Chrome.

I'm now used to having the tabs up on the title bar since all the other modern browsers are arranged this way. Brave has the classical arrangement with the tabs below the navigation bar.

The active tab changes color with the pages theme. This is cool, but I wish the inactive tabs persisted the same colors as I switch tabs instead of just changing to grey. Not a big deal at all but there are a lot of little things like this that I just wondered why they didn't do it just slightly differently.

It comes with HTTPS Everywhere and UBlock Origin built in by default, which is good.

Downloading files works like normal and the file appears on a bottom bar just like in Chrome, except after the file is downloaded there is no option to open the file directly. Instead when you mouse over the file options appear for redownload, copy link location, open file folder, or delete the download. One of those little things - why not let me open the file directly?

Edit - One other thing I forgot. I'm used to being able to drag a tab to another monitor to view as a separate window. I use that feature a lot and it doesn't work that way in Brave. You can drag the tab but I'm not sure what the purpose is since you can't do anything with it.

.

.

TLDR; All in all it feels like a promising but unfinished browser.
